title: (Scenario) The consumer app is running with no errors, but messages sit in the topic unconsumed: how do you diagnose it: (1) the consumer group ALREADY committed those offsets (Kafka doesn't redeliver: reset offsets or use a new group.id), (2) auto.offset.reset=latest on a brand-new group SKIPPED all pre-existing messages (set earliest if you need the backlog), (3) more consumers than partitions so some consumers are IDLE (a partition is owned by exactly one consumer per group), or (4) the group is stuck rebalancing: and which tools confirm it (kafka-consumer-groups --describe to see per-partition CURRENT-OFFSET/LOG-END-OFFSET/LAG and member assignment)?
shortTitle: (Scenario) The consumer app is running with no errors, but messages sit in the topic unconsumed: how do you diagnose it?

s1_definition.oneliner: Unconsumed-but-no-errors is usually already-committed offsets, a latest reset skipping the backlog, more consumers than partitions leaving some idle, or a stuck rebalance, and consumer-groups describe shows the offsets, lag, and assignment that tell you which.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Already committed** -- Kafka does not redeliver committed messages to the same group; the fix is to reset offsets or use a new group.id.
- **Latest reset** -- a brand-new group with `auto.offset.reset=latest` silently skips all pre-existing messages; set `earliest` for the backlog.
- **Idle consumers** -- more consumers than partitions means some sit idle because a partition is owned by exactly one consumer per group.
- **Stuck rebalance** -- members keep joining and leaving, so the group never settles into stable assignment and processes little.
- **Diagnostic tool** -- `kafka-consumer-groups --describe` shows per-partition current offset, log-end offset, lag, member assignment, and group state.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine transfer slips piling up in a tray at National Bank of India while the clerk insists they are working fine. Maybe the clerk already stamped those slips as done earlier. Maybe a new clerk was told to only handle slips arriving after they sat down, so the old pile is invisible. Maybe there are five clerks but only three trays, so two clerks sit idle. Or maybe the team is reshuffling who owns which tray and nobody is actually working yet.

```text
 Diagnostic Decision Tree
 =========================

 Consumer running, no errors, messages unconsumed
                    │
                    ▼
     kafka-consumer-groups --describe
                    │
         ┌──────────┴──────────┐
         │                     │
    LAG = 0                LAG > 0
    everywhere             on some partitions
         │                     │
         ▼                     ▼
  Cause 1: Already       ┌─────────────────┐
  committed              │ CURRENT-OFFSET=0 │
  Fix: reset offsets     │ on high-lag      │
  or new group.id        │ partitions?      │
                         └────┬────────────┘
                         yes  │        no
                              │        │
                    ┌─────────┘    ┌───┴──────────┐
                    ▼              │ CONSUMER-ID   │
              Cause 2: latest     │ missing?      │
              reset skipped       └──┬────────────┘
              backlog              yes│       no
              Fix: set earliest       │        │
                                     ▼        ▼
                              Cause 3/4:   Check:
                              Idle or      - Topic name typo?
                              rebalancing  - Processing too slow?
                              Check group
                              state field
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
When a consumer runs cleanly but messages sit unconsumed, I look at offsets, membership, and assignment, not at a crash. The four classic causes are: the group already committed those offsets, a brand-new group with latest reset skipped the backlog, more consumers than partitions leaving some idle, or a stuck rebalance.

The diagnostic tool is `kafka-consumer-groups --describe`, which shows per-partition current offset, log-end offset, lag, and member assignment. LAG of zero means the group already consumed everything. High lag with a current offset of zero points to a latest reset. Missing consumer IDs point to idle consumers or a rebalance.

In my National Bank of India work, a new reconciliation consumer appeared to process nothing. The describe output showed large lag with offset zero and latest reset on a fresh group. We changed to earliest, reset offsets, and the backlog drained immediately.

Remember one sentence: use kafka-consumer-groups --describe to check lag, current offset, and member assignment, because unconsumed messages with no errors is always an offset, membership, or assignment problem.

---

keyPoints: Kafka does not redeliver committed messages; reset offsets or use a new group.id to reprocess.
A new group with auto.offset.reset=latest silently skips all existing messages in the topic.
More consumers than partitions means some sit idle because each partition is owned by one consumer.
A stuck rebalance from flapping or slow processing prevents stable partition assignment.
kafka-consumer-groups --describe shows per-partition current offset, log-end offset, lag, and member assignment.
Check the group state field to distinguish Stable from PreparingRebalance.
